consistency.evidence: adjacent frames leave 4.2% of pixels changed after a global translation, and 3.3% of 24px blocks still differ (worst window 3.3%) -- one rigid scene accounts for the change

matching.reason: retrieval matching against 21 keyframes costs 1554 pairs against 3570 exhaustive (43.5%); the sequential window alone would cost 795 pairs and find no revisits
unmatched_notes: sequential matching compares only the 10 nearest temporal neighbours, so any two views more than 10 samples apart are not matched by it; on this walk the largest such gap is 42 samples

retrieval matching compares each frame against 21 keyframes, so a revisit matches only if one of its frames is near a keyframe in appearance; a short revisit in a visually distinct part of the room can still be missed
a loop closure missed here shows up as two disconnected reconstructions, not as a bad one: check the registration report before treating a sparse model as a single room

findings.measured: median global translation explains 2% of the frame change
findings.cause: the picture changes without the camera translating, which is a pan, a zoom or a handheld wobble; those give no depth
findings.action: keep translating while turning; translate the camera body, not just the view

notes: frame target 150, selected 85 (hypothesis 100-200 frames for a small room -- a starting point, not a guarantee).
resolution is reported, never used as a rejection: 720p matches features, it only softens distance
